output.answer_markdown: Kroger says it is subject to commodity price risk generated by its purchases of meat, seafood and dairy products, among other food items [1]. The price and availability of these commodities directly affect its results of operations [2]. To help manage this exposure, it uses pricing features in supply contracts, such as fixed-price and price-to-be-fixed contracts, and can increase or decrease retail prices as commodity prices change [3]. Kroger is also exposed to changes in diesel and unleaded fuel prices, and most of its fuel contracts use index-based pricing formulas plus or minus a fixed locational/supplier differential [4][5]. As of January 29, 2022 and January 30, 2021, Kroger had no commodity derivative contracts outstanding [6].
